environment.description: Same IoT message handler on same EC2 instance, but origin is NOT publicly accessible. Security group sg-0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8 ingress rules restrict port 443 to AWS CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing, pl-3b927c52). CloudFront distribution d1a2b3c4d5e6f7.cloudfront.net is configured with a custom origin (ALB DNS) and has Restrict Viewer Access enabled (Trusted Key Group: kg-iot-prod-2024 with RSA-2048 key pair). All requests require valid CloudFront signed URLs with policy conditions: URL must match /api/v1/messages/ingest path pattern only, DateLessThan constraint of 300 seconds, and IpAddress condition restricting to the IoT gateway CIDR 10.200.0.0/16. The /api/v1/devices/lookup path is NOT included in any canned or custom policy — CloudFront returns 403 for any signed URL attempting to access it. Origin Access settings use Origin Shield in us-east-1 with custom header X-Origin-Verify containing a rotating secret validated by ALB listener rule (returns 403 fixed response if header missing/invalid).

config.network: SG ingress limited to CloudFront prefix list pl-3b927c52 only
config.cdn: CloudFront d1a2b3c4d5e6f7.cloudfront.net, Restrict Viewer Access ON
config.signing: Trusted Key Group kg-iot-prod-2024, RSA-2048, custom policy
config.origin_shield: us-east-1, custom header X-Origin-Verify with rotating secret
config.alb_rule: Listener rule priority 1: if X-Origin-Verify != current_secret then fixed-response 403
config.vulnerable_endpoint_access: /api/v1/devices/lookup is not covered by any signed URL policy
